verification.reason: The code path is real. `Install.read` takes the outermost ancestor holding a `node_modules` as root (installed-packages.ts:52-53). For a global install, that is `/usr/local/lib`, and `#scan` walks every global package under it. With the default `past = "fails"`, `#scan` throws once more than 50,000 directories are entered (206-210). `melianInstall()` (code-version.ts:29) uses that default. Its callers (lens-request.ts:129, checks.ts:734, adjudication.ts:425, dismiss.ts:243, doctor.ts:242) have no catch that lets the review continue. So a review, a dismiss or doctor would fail wherever the root widens past the bound. At base, nothing walked the install: `piVersions` read two package versions, so the same install reviewed normally. The bound is chosen deliberately, not a slip. The decision at head, `2026-11-20-keys-hold-installed-packages.md`, says a global install rooted at `/usr/lib` "fails closed". It also says "Melian's own install still fails at the bound". That decision exists only at head. Its own reason for loosening the bound for the instrumenter's install, that an ordinary layout the base reviewed must not abort every review, applies equally here. What I cannot trace is whether real global installs or stray `~/node_modules` exceed 50,000 directories. That needs a run against such a layout. The failure is therefore reachable but depends on the environment. The `list_mutants` install was given the unidentified fallback, and Melian's own install was not.
